narrative.overview: uExel's page reads like a confident engineering firm's own materials: a near-black control-room base, one signal-blue accent doing all the pointing, and condensed technical numerals stamped on everything from stat counters to case-study indices. The signature move is literal — cards for expertise areas and service categories sit tilted at odd angles (-8 deg/+8 deg), as if scattered spec sheets on a drafting table rather than snapped into a rigid grid. A canvas-particle animation dissolves and reforms the hero's closing word, the one moment of overt spectacle in an otherwise disciplined, restrained system. The system rejects decorative color and heavy shadow: outside the signal-blue accent and its navy-gradient companions, everything is near-black, white, or muted gray, and most surfaces sit flat with soft diffuse elevation reserved for a handful of interactive surfaces.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black + navy base, one signal-blue accent, no other hues
Abel (condensed uppercase display) for numerals and headings, Inter for body copy
Tilted "fanned" cards as the recurring signature motif
Pill-shaped CTAs contrast deliberately with sharp-cornered data tags
Flat by default; shadow appears only on a small set of elevated interactive surfaces

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is the only hue in the system besides navy and near-black/white. Reach for Signal Blue or a tint of it before introducing anything else.

rules.name: The Text-on-Fill Rule
rules.body: Any white text sitting directly on a blue fill uses the darker Signal Blue (Button) variant (#0972b8), never plain Signal Blue (#0b7ec9).

rules.name: The All-Caps Numerals Rule
rules.body: Every numeral meant to carry visual weight sits in Abel and is treated as a graphic element, never rendered in Inter.

rules.name: The Flat-First Rule
rules.body: Default every new surface to no shadow. Add a named shadow only when the element genuinely floats above other content.

rules.name: The Pill-or-Sharp Rule
rules.body: A rounded element is either fully pill-shaped (actions) or sits at the established 10-14px card/field scale (containers). Data chips are the one deliberate 0px exception.

dos: Do keep Signal Blue as the only accent hue; reach for a tint/shade of it before introducing a new color.
Do use the darker Signal Blue (Button) variant, not plain Signal Blue, anywhere white text sits directly on a blue fill.
Do keep the tilted-card motif (±8°, alternating direction) for any new browsable-options card grouping.
Do default new surfaces to no shadow; add a named shadow only for genuinely floating/elevated elements.
Do use Abel for numerals and headings, Inter for everything read as a sentence.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue without a deliberate decision — the system currently has none, on purpose.
Don't use a mid-range border-radius (6-8px) on any container; commit to either a full pill or the established 10-14px scale.
Don't apply the tilted-card treatment to content that isn't a browsable grouping of options.
Don't treat --radius: 22px as a real, load-bearing token — it's currently unused; resolve or remove it rather than building on it.
